acceptance: Every failed cell of the 2026-11-22 timeseries trunk UAT shard is named with its cause, and failed cells are named in the job log.
context: Filed 2026-11-22 while closing out the run-timeout follow-ups (umbrella run-timeout-plan-20261120). Evidence was read on 2026-11-22; re-read run logs, file paths and line numbers before acting.
description:
## Problem
Trunk UAT run 45007293835 (develop 93f336032a, 2026-11-22) failed job `UAT stage 3 timeseries` (137161944469): the `release-gate-03-docker-oltp` summary shows `phase_exit_codes` execute 1 and report 1, while the visible QuestDB cells (tsbs_devops, nyctaxi, flightdata, datavault at SF 0.01) published results; `make uat-sweep` exited with Error 1. The job log names no failing cell; the cell results are in the shard artifact and the runner's `log_dir` `/home/runner/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_20261122_094514`. Trunk UAT failed on 4 of the 6 runs from 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-22; open items exist for some other failures (cedardb-server-crash-mid-shard-nightly-20261119, clickhouse-local-tpchavoc-sf1-timeout-nightly-20261119).

## Change
From the shard artifact, name each failed cell and its error. Fix the cause, or record it on the matching existing item. Separately, make the UAT summary print the failed cells and their exit status in the job log.

## Decision gates
- Do not mark cells flaky or skip them without a recorded cause.
- Keep BenchBox's `timed-out` (exit 124) distinct from the runner's `hung` outside kill; do not change either limit without the owner.
- Live cloud platforms are out of scope.

## Verification rubric
Pass: each failed cell of this run named with its cause on this item; a fix or a link to the item that owns it; a test or log line showing that a failed cell is named in the job log; the next timeseries shard run green or failing only on a tracked cause.
Fail: cause unrecorded.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
